death.note: doxologia.ro: her akathist «a fost găsit într-un codice din anul 1455, unde se consemnează că sfânta a murit înainte de această dată». The page gives no year of death.

feast.note: Doxologia keeps her twice: its calendar prints her on 15 iulie and again on 20 octombrie — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Matrona din Chios». One attestation row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. Both days link the same doxologia page, which says she is kept on 20 octombrie and on 15 iulie, the day her head was found; 15 iulie is the day this folder was read from. Read 25 September 2026.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 15 iulie — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Matrona din Chios»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 20ης Οκτωβρίου — «Οσία Ματρώνα η Χιοπολίτιδα, η θαυματουργή»

attestations.note: The life page `https://www.saint.gr/812/saint.aspx` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 20 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους». That is not the day the folder's Romanian row keeps — doxologia.ro has her on 15 iulie — but the two rows are two churches, and the entry is plainly the same woman: Maria of the village of Volissos on Chios, daughter of Leon and Anna, youngest of seven sisters, tonsured Matrona and made abbess against her will. The page dates her repose 1462 and then argues against itself: «Άλλες πηγές υπολογίζουν τον χρόνο κοιμήσεως της Αγίας 100 περίπου χρόνια πριν το 1462, διότι η πρώτη βιογραφία της γράφτηκε από τον Μητροπολίτη Ρόδου Νείλο (1357)», which is why the folder's existing `before 1455` is left untouched rather than replaced by 1462. It puts her skull at Zographou and her right hand at Dionysiou on Athos, and notes that because abbesses were called κυρά she is still called Αγία Κυρά, whence the names Κυράτσω and Κερασιά keep this day. Its Ἀπολυτίκιον and Κοντάκιον are taken; two Μεγαλυνάρια are not a kind the schema holds. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Urmând în pașii lui Hristos, ai renunțat la plăcerile lumii, Cuvioasă, și în trup ai imitat viața îngerilor. Prin urmare, ai umplut Chiosul, insula ta natală, de bucurie și de darurile dăruite de Sfântul Duh, Prea-lăudată fecioară. Prin urmare, strigăm cu bucurie: „Bucură-te, Prea-binecuvântată Matrona.”

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintei Cuvioase Matrona» — the page prints no glas.

english.text: Following in the steps of Christ you gave up the pleasures of the world, venerable one, and in the body you imitated the life of the angels. And so you filled Chios, the island of your birth, with joy and with the gifts of the Holy Spirit, all-praised virgin. And so we cry out with joy: Rejoice, most blessed Matrona.

hymns.text: Χριστοῦ τοῖς ἴχνεσιν, ἀκολουθήσασα, κόσμου τερπνότητα, Ὁσία ἔλιπες, καὶ ἐμιμήσω ἐν σαρκί, Ἀγγέλων τὴν πολιτείαν· ὅθεν ταῖς τοῦ Πνεύματος, δωρεαῖς κατεφαίδρυνας, τὴν ἐνεγκαμένην σε, νῆσον Χίον πανεύφημε· διὸ χαρμονικῶς ἐκβοᾷ σοι· χαίροις Ματρῶνα πανολβία.

source.text: saint.gr, «Οσία Ματρώνα η Χιοπολίτιδα, η θαυματουργή» — Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’. Τὴν ὡραιότητα

english.text: Following the footsteps of Christ, venerable one, you left behind the delight of the world and imitated in the flesh the manner of life of the angels; and so with the gifts of the Spirit you made bright the island of Chios that bore you, all-praised one. And so it cries out to you with joy: Rejoice, Matrona, all-blessed.

hymns.text: Οὐδαμῶς τὸ θῆλύ σοι, ἐμποδὼν ὤφθη Ματρῶνα, πρὸς τοὺς ὑπὲρ ἄνθρωπον, ἀγῶνας ὄντως καὶ ἄθλους· ᾔσχυνας, διὸ τὸν μέγαν νοῦν θεοφόρε· εὔφρανας, τὸ γυναικεῖον μεγάλως γένος, τὸ ἐκείνου ταῖς σαῖς νίκαις, προσαφελοῦσα τῆς ἥττης ὄνειδος.

source.text: saint.gr, «Οσία Ματρώνα η Χιοπολίτιδα, η θαυματουργή» — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’ (the page prints no model)

english.text: Your womanhood was no hindrance to you at all, Matrona, in struggles and contests truly beyond the strength of man; and so, God-bearer, you put the great mind to shame, and greatly gladdened the race of women, taking from it by your victories the reproach of defeat.
